title: Classical training helped him; losing a job to a bluesy trumpeter
summary: He came west to play classical music; he says the training helped and he was fired when a trumpeter who played blues drew the crowd.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Okay, in that period you were on -- around 15. So what happened, would you still play, in what was it. What was your hometown again?
Steubenville, Ohio.
Then you decided to come to the West Coast?
Yeah, we come to the West Coast. About much older
How old were you?
Yeah, to play classical music.
You were trained classically, right.
Right.
So was that a problem when you started to play jazz?
No. It helped a whole lot. I'm sure, with the background.
It helped. You mentioned that trumpet player came in and he could slide the notes around, he could play the bluesy notes. Remember that story.
Yeah, I remember it, but I don't know who it was now.
Can't say the name, but you knew that you were going to lose your job because of the way he was playing.
Oh, yeah, I did lose my job too.
What happened?
Only thing, I just got fired.
Because the other player played more like what they wanted?
Yeah, played more like they wanted. And had the -- what do you call, the guests, following him around.
The people?
Yeah, people.
You mean the audience liked what he
was doing.
Yeah.
Did you feel a little uncomfortable because of what he could do and --
No, not at all.
But you knew you were going to lose your job?
Yeah, I knew I was going to lose it.
That hurt a little bit, didn't it?
No, it didn't bother me.
Because you were going to lose your job?
No.
It didn't bother you.
Didn't bother me at all. I think we better get off that.
Want to move on?
Yeah, I don't know enough about it to tell you.
